newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul Red Cross offers North new food aid talks.
newsitem.headline: Seoul Red Cross offers North new food aid talks.

text.p: South Korea's Red Cross on Saturday offered new talks with its North Korean counterpart on supplying more food aid to the hunger-stricken nation.
The Red Cross statement said the offer of talks for July 22 was made over the border hot-line. The border village of Panmunjom was proposed as the venue.
Red Cross societies of the two Koreas signed an agreement in May in Beijing to ship 50,000 tonnes of food aid, mostly corn, to the North by the end of July.
Trains carrying the first shipments of food aid entered the North on June 12.

Kang Young-hoon, president of the South Korean Red Cross, was quoted in the statement as saying the last batch of aid and an additional 2,000 tonnes of fertiliser would be delivered to port of Nampo from July 21 to 28.
International aid agencies are stepping up food appeals for the North, warning of imminent starvation particularly among young children who are most at risk.
